review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

4:1.sourceText: Τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ῥητῶς λέγει ὅτι ἐν ὑστέροις καιροῖς ἀποστήσονταί τινες τῆς πίστεως, προσέχοντες πνεύμασιν πλάνοις καὶ διδασκαλίαις δαιμονίων,
4:1.targetText: And the Spirit expressly says that in latter times some will depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and teachings of demons,

4:2.sourceText: ἐν ὑποκρίσει ψευδολόγων, κεκαυστηριασμένων τὴν ἰδίαν συνείδησιν,
4:2.targetText: speaking lies in hypocrisy, being seared in their own conscience,

groups.note: The Greek genitive plural liar/false-speaker designation ψευδολόγων is recast as speaking lies; the action comes from that actual compound designation, not an invented speaking infinitive.
The accusative conscience phrase marks the respect/sphere of the searing; English uses in their own conscience. No separate Greek in is printed at that second location.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:3.sourceText: κωλυόντων γαμεῖν, ἀπέχεσθαι βρωμάτων, ἃ ὁ Θεὸς ἔκτισεν εἰς μετάλημψιν μετὰ εὐχαριστίας τοῖς πιστοῖς καὶ ἐπεγνωκόσι τὴν ἀλήθειαν.
4:3.targetText: forbidding to marry—to abstain from meats that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those believing and acknowledging the truth,

groups.note: The preposition plus reception noun εἰς μετάλημψιν, for reception, is rendered as a purpose infinitive to be received; the actual reception noun and purpose relation jointly support it.

The Greek dative faithful/believing designation supplies the beneficiaries/recipients of food reception; LSV gives by those believing. The English by recasts this dative recipient as the receiver, without a source by preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

review.note: The Greek first forbids marriage and then gives to abstain from foods with an understood demanding/enjoining relation. LSV marks the shift with a dash; no extra commanding verb is invented or transferred onto forbidding.

4:4.sourceText: ὅτι πᾶν κτίσμα Θεοῦ καλόν, καὶ οὐδὲν ἀπόβλητον μετὰ εὐχαριστίας λαμβανόμενον·
4:4.targetText: because every creature of God [is] good, and nothing [is] to be rejected, with thanksgiving being received,

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

4:5.sourceText: ἁγιάζεται γὰρ διὰ λόγου Θεοῦ καὶ ἐντεύξεως.
4:5.targetText: for it is sanctified through the word of God and intercession.

4:6.sourceText: Ταῦτα ὑποτιθέμενος τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς καλὸς ἔσῃ διάκονος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ἐντρεφόμενος τοῖς λόγοις τῆς πίστεως καὶ τῆς καλῆς διδασκαλίας ᾗ παρηκολούθηκας·
4:6.targetText: Placing these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Jesus Christ, being nourished by the words of the faith, and of the good teaching, which you followed after,

review.note: The Jesus/Christ title order is reversed in displayed LSV relative to N1904 Christ Jesus; each actual name/title retains its own identity.

4:7.sourceText: τοὺς δὲ βεβήλους καὶ γραώδεις μύθους παραιτοῦ. γύμναζε δὲ σεαυτὸν πρὸς εὐσέβειαν.
4:7.targetText: but reject the profane and old women’s fables, and exercise yourself to piety,

4:8.sourceText: ἡ γὰρ σωματικὴ γυμνασία πρὸς ὀλίγον ἐστὶν ὠφέλιμος· ἡ δὲ εὐσέβεια πρὸς πάντα ὠφέλιμός ἐστιν, ἐπαγγελίαν ἔχουσα ζωῆς τῆς νῦν καὶ τῆς μελλούσης.
4:8.targetText: for bodily exercise is to little profit, but piety is profitable to all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is coming;

groups.note: The adjective ὠφέλιμος means profitable/useful; LSV recasts the predicate as is to little profit, retaining the benefit head as the English noun profit.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies is in the life that now is; Greek has an article plus now without a being verb. The later is coming belongs to the actual coming participle.

4:9.sourceText: πιστὸς ὁ λόγος καὶ πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος·
4:9.targetText: the word [is] steadfast, and worthy of all acceptance;

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

4:10.sourceText: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ κοπιῶμεν καὶ ἀγωνιζόμεθα, ὅτι ἠλπίκαμεν ἐπὶ Θεῷ ζῶντι, ὅς ἐστιν Σωτὴρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων, μάλιστα πιστῶν.
4:10.targetText: for this we both labor and are reproached, because we hope on the living God, who is Savior of all men—especially of those believing.

groups.note: The one written coordinating καί links the two predicates; English frames their coordination as both ... and. This shared connector does not equate the unlike second lexical predicates.
The genitive plural believing/faithful adjective is substantive, rendered of those believing; those expresses its people reference, not an independently printed Greek demonstrative.

unmappedSource.reason: The explanatory conjunction γάρ has no separate English counterpart when LSV contracts the Greek for-to-this transition to for this. The actual purpose/direction preposition supplies for.
Source-witness predicate difference: N1904 ἀγωνιζόμεθα means we struggle/strive, while LSV are reproached follows TR ὀνειδιζόμεθα.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness predicate difference: LSV are reproached is TR ὀνειδιζόμεθα, not pinned N1904 we struggle/strive.

4:12.sourceText: μηδείς σου τῆς νεότητος καταφρονείτω, ἀλλὰ τύπος γίνου τῶν πιστῶν ἐν λόγῳ, ἐν ἀναστροφῇ, ἐν ἀγάπῃ, ἐν πίστει, ἐν ἁγνείᾳ.
4:12.targetText: let no one despise your youth, but become a pattern of those believing in word, in behavior, in love, in spirit, in faith, in purity;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness phrase addition: LSV in spirit follows extra TR ἐν πνεύματι between love and faith; pinned N1904 has no such phrase.

4:13.sourceText: ἕως ἔρχομαι πρόσεχε τῇ ἀναγνώσει, τῇ παρακλήσει, τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ.
4:13.targetText: until I come, give heed to the reading, to the exhortation, to the teaching;

4:14.sourceText: μὴ ἀμέλει τοῦ ἐν σοὶ χαρίσματος, ὃ ἐδόθη σοι διὰ προφητείας μετὰ ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τοῦ πρεσβυτερίου.
4:14.targetText: do not be careless of the gift in you, that was given you through prophecy, with laying on of the hands of the eldership;

4:15.sourceText: ταῦτα μελέτα, ἐν τούτοις ἴσθι, ἵνα σου ἡ προκοπὴ φανερὰ ᾖ πᾶσιν.
4:15.targetText: be careful of these things; be in these things, that your advancement may be evident in all things;

groups.note: The practicing/attending imperative μελέτα is rendered be careful of, an English attentiveness idiom, without a separate Greek be or of word.

Pinned N1904 has dative πᾶσιν, all/everyone, without a head noun or preposition. LSV construes all respects/things and follows TR extra ἐν as in all things. The actual all quantifier is retained with this construal difference explicit; the absent preposition is separately unpaired.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness preposition addition: LSV in all things follows extra TR ἐν before πᾶσιν; pinned N1904 has only the dative all/everyone.

4:16.sourceText: ἔπεχε σεαυτῷ καὶ τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ, ἐπίμενε αὐτοῖς· τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν καὶ σεαυτὸν σώσεις καὶ τοὺς ἀκούοντάς σου.
4:16.targetText: take heed to yourself and to the teaching; remain in them, for doing this thing, you will save both yourself and those hearing you.
